title: Introduce causal token attribution matrix and alert hysteresis for noisy SLOs
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a causal token attribution matrix to the telemetry pipeline and new alert hysteresis logic to reduce SLO alert churn. Includes dashboard panels and docs for on-call runbooks.
description: Motivation: High-frequency SLO alerts from token-level cost spikes were noisy and hard to triage because surface metrics attributed cost/latency to endpoints only. This change introduces a causal token attribution matrix that attributes token-phase cost and latency back to callsite and prompt regions and a hysteresis-based alert attenuation layer to reduce alert churn without losing signal. Scope: 1) runtime telemetry: enrich spans with token-phase attribution and causal weights; 2) metrics pipeline: aggregate causal matrices into compact histograms and per-route rollups; 3) alerting: new hysteresis DAG that applies smoothing and minimum-stability windows before firing; 4) dashboards: attribution matrix panel, per-tenant token-fingerprint sparkline, and an alert-churn diagnostics page; 5) docs and runbook: guidance for tuning hysteresis knobs. Checklist: [x] runtime span enrichment implemented [x] pipeline aggregation and compact histogram schema added [x] dashboard panels and example queries [x] unit and integration tests [x] runbook and docs update [x] CI green Context and rationale: customers running bursty LLM workloads reported repeated alerts during ephemeral token-cost surges caused by a small number of high-entropy tokens in prompt templates. The causal matrix lets us correlate which token-phase (prompt, system, candidate, post-filter) and which prompt region is responsible for downstream token cost/latency while the hysteresis layer prevents transient spikes from immediately paging on-call. Backwards compatibility: all enriched span fields are optional at ingest time; older consumers ignore the new attributes. Implementation notes: - Runtime: added a lightweight token attribution hook in the serving runtime that emits a token-attrib span tag with a compact base64-encoded vector of 4 phase weights and a 32-bit fingerprint for prompt region. - Aggregation: new pipeline stage 'causal-matrix-compactify' that quantizes and reservoir-samples attribution vectors and increments multires histograms. - Metrics: two new metric families: redwood.token_attrib.rollup and redwood.token_attrib.heatmap_count with labels route, tenant, phase, quantile_bin. - Alerting: alert hysteresis introduced as an ordered policy chain (stability-window->decay-rate->coalesce) configurable per-tenant and per-route. - Dashboards: attribution matrix uses a density heatmap with reweighted color scale and an interactive token-fingerprint drilldown that joins samples to sparse logs. - Docs: added runbook with recommended knob defaults and debugging steps. Testing: unit tests for compactifier and histogram ingestion, integration test that replays synthetic invocations and verifies alert suppression behavior, and dashboard CI snapshots. Migration: rollout is opt-in via feature flag telemetry.token_attrib.v1; default off for private deployments for 2 weeks while we validate. Related work: follows up on ENG-4201 (kv-cache profiler) and SRE-220 regarding alert fatigue. See SUP-1021 for customer-reported incidents. Commits summary: 1) Add attribution hook and serializer 2) Add pipeline compactifier and metrics exporter 3) Add alert hysteresis policy and tests 4) Dashboard panels and queries 5) Docs and runbook Changes (high-level): - runtime/trace/attr_hook.go: new token attribution hook and deterministic fingerprinting - telemetry/pipeline/compactifier.py: quantization + reservoir sampler - telemetry/metrics/exporter.go: new metrics families and mapping - observability/dashboards/token_attribution.json: new panels and templating - alerts/alert_policies.go: hysteresis policy implementation and config knobs - tests/telemetry/test_compactifier.py: unit tests - tests/integration/test_hysteresis_replay.py: integration replay test Review summary: initial review requested improvement to knob names and default window sizes. Addressed by renaming stability_window_ms -> stability_window and lowering default from 60000ms to 20000ms after a small canary run showed latency to be safe. CI: initial run had one flaky dashboard snapshot mismatch on Windows runner; fixed by normalizing timezone and re-ran. Merge: squash and merge after approvals.
